## Maintainer ruling — Option C

Ruled by the maintainer in a live PM session, 2026-08-13 (session `session_015XyMgCSMGGn9oSwbQEeWYg`), verbatim: 「其他全部接受你的建议。」 — accepting the recommendation presented there, restated below so this card is self-contained.

**Ruling: C — the state is legal with declared fail-closed semantics, plus a targeted signup-ordering fix.**

1. **Declared rule (ADR-class):** under an authenticated session with `activeOrganizationId == null`, tenant-scoped **reads resolve to nothing** and tenant-scoped **writes are refused loudly** (4xx naming the missing active organization). ⛔ No silent NULL stamping anywhere.
2. **Signup ordering:** membership settles synchronously before the first session mints (or the first-session ledger rows' tenant is back-filled once the session gains its org) — account-creation audit rows are exactly what a bare fail-closed refusal would permanently lose.
3. #8158's landed reject-direction fix conforms and stands.

**Implementation notes for dispatch:**
- The ADR draft is part of the implementation card: AI drafts, pushes, opens the PR — ⛔ the ADR PR is merged by the maintainer only, never queued or auto-merged.
- #8208 (silent NULL stamp → becomes a 4xx refusal) and #8245 (NULL-tenant audit rows → covered by the ordering fix / back-fill) are dispositioned by this ruling; direction comments left on both.
- Re-run the card's premise re-checks at claim time (signup ordering still live; PR #8237 merged).

Label swap: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`.

## Claim

Claimed by the dev seat, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`, branch `claude/issue-8247-no-active-org-semantics`.

Implementing the maintainer's **Option C** ruling (comment above). Re-reading the card's comments before the first edit; no earlier claim comment with a different session ID is present.

### Premise re-checks (ruling asks for both)

- **PR #8237 merged** — confirmed: `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-08-12T22:35:13Z`, merged by `os-zhuang`, base `main`. ✅
- **Signup ordering still live** — being re-measured now against `origin/main` @ `1d1ca8e99`. Static read so far: `AuthManager.composeDatabaseHooks` still composes the ADR-0093 reconciler into `user.create.after` and `defaultActiveOrg` into `session.create.before`, and `defaultActiveOrg` still returns early (leaving `activeOrganizationId` null) when no `sys_member` row resolves. No synchronous-settle change has landed in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src` since the card was filed. Reporting the measured half in the dev report.

### Declared file surface (pre-first-edit; re-checked against in-flight branches)

Expected to touch, in this repo only:

- `docs/adr/0123-*.md` — the ADR-class declared rule (rule 1). New file.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/` — the write half of rule 1 (the read half already fails closed in `tenant-layer.ts`: `computeTenantLayer0Filter` returns `RLS_DENY_FILTER` on a walled posture with no active org). Plus its tests.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/` — rule 2, signup ordering.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/` — rule 2, ledger tenant back-fill, if the ordering fix alone does not cover it.
- `.changeset/*.md`.

⚠️ `packages/plugins/plugin-security` is named by my dispatch as a possible other-lane package. I am measuring whether the write refusal is **irreducibly** there before writing anything into it, and will report the irreducible per-lane surface to the PM rather than widening silently.

### PR shape

Prime Directive #14 reserves the landing of any `docs/adr/**` diff to the maintainer, and the PM seat cannot arm or queue such a PR. I will state the chosen shape and the reasoning in the dev report and in the PR bodies.

## Dev report — #8247 (session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`)

```json
{
  "issue": 8247,
  "status": "done",
  "branch": "claude/issue-8247-no-active-org-semantics + claude/issue-8247-signup-membership-ordering",
  "pr": "https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/8471 (ADR-0123 + rule 1, maintainer-merge only) · https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/8473 (rule 2, normal flow)",
  "premise_still_valid": true
}
```

### Premise re-checks (verbatim)

1. **PR #8237 merged** — YES. `state: closed`, `merged: true`, `merged_at: 2026-08-12T22:35:13Z`, `merged_by: os-zhuang`, base `main`, head `claude/issue-8158-admin-org-scope-fall-open`.
2. **Signup ordering still live** — YES, on `origin/main` @ `1d1ca8e99`. `AuthManager.composeDatabaseHooks` still composes the ADR-0093 reconciler into `user.create.after` and `defaultActiveOrg` into `session.create.before`, and `defaultActiveOrg` still `return`s with the field unset when no `sys_member` row resolves. `git log -6 origin/main -- packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src` shows no synchronous-settle change. The repo states the premise in its own words, in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/auth-session-audit-trail.dogfood.test.ts`:

   > `session.create.before` derives `activeOrganizationId` from the caller's `sys_member` row, and ADR-0093's reconciler runs on `user.create.after`, which better-auth defers past the signup transaction. So a user's very FIRST session — the one sign-up mints — legitimately predates their membership and carries no active org; its ledger row therefore has no tenant, and no seam downstream can invent one.

Neither premise has moved. Nothing to stop on.

### PR shape — two PRs, and the split is forced rather than chosen

| PR | Contents | Landing |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **#8471** | `docs/adr/0123-*` + rule 1's enforcement in `plugin-security` + 19 tests + changeset | ⛔ maintainer only |
| **#8473** | rule 2's ordering fix in `plugin-auth` + 13 tests + changeset | normal flow |

The mechanical reason, measured: **`check:adr-anchors` requires every `ADR-NNNN` in a tracked file to name a real record under `docs/adr/`** (script header, line 90). Prime Directive #13 requires code realizing an ADR's decision to carry its id. So rule 1's enforcement — which cites ADR-0123 — *cannot* be in a different PR from the ADR; CI would reject it. Rule 2 has no such coupling: it stands on already-accepted **ADR-0093**, cites no unmerged record, and closes #8245 regardless of how ADR-0123's text is finally worded.

The judgement call the dispatch left to me was "is the code meaningful before the ADR ratifies it". Split per half: **rule 1 is the semantics** (a new decision in ADR-0095/0105 territory, wire-visible on a security boundary) and is meaningless without its record; **rule 2 is a bug fix** that is correct under any of options A/B/C. The landing order is also favourable — #8473 *reduces how often* the state occurs at signup, before #8471 starts refusing writes in it.

### Do rules 1 and 2 measurably close #8208 and #8245?

**#8245 — YES, measured end to end.** `loginEventFor` reads `session.activeOrganizationId`; with the ordering fixed there is one to read. Pinned by feeding the hook's own output to `loginEventFor` and asserting the tenant. Ablation: that pin goes red on `origin/main`.

**#8208 — YES at the enforcement layer, and #8471 declares `Fixes #8208`.** Its defect ("stamped `organization_id: NULL`, immediately invisible to its own creator") requires the write to *land*; under rule 1 it is refused first. Ablation on the pre-fix build: `the write was not refused at all: expected undefined to be defined`.

⚠️ **Residual honesty on #8208:** I did not write an HTTP-level pin. The `PermissionDeniedError → 403` mapping is pre-existing. See the dogfood item below, which is probably that measurement arriving for free — but I have **not** proven it.

### Ablation — predictions written before mutating, then compared

Predictions file written before the first edit; both mutations run against the committed fix (never `git stash`).

| # | Prediction | Measured | Match |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | insert refused → RED | RED | ✅ |
| A2 | update refused → RED | RED | ✅ |
| A3 | read-side pins stay GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| A4 | existing forge-guard pins stay GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| A5 | system / platform / single-posture controls GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| — | *(A totals)* | **6 red / 13 green**, all 6 write-refusal pins | ✅ |
| B1 | first session carries org → RED | RED | ✅ |
| B2 | login audit event carries tenant → RED | RED | ✅ |
| B3 | `invite-only` binds nobody → GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| B4 | no target org → GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| B5 | pre-existing membership unchanged → GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| B6 | host hook precedence → GREEN | GREEN | ✅ |
| — | *(B totals)* | **2 red / 11 green** | ✅ |

No inverted direction and no "more diagnostics" shape in either run; both were plain RED, which is what a refusal that feeds no count should produce.

**How empty-by-rule was separated from empty-by-accident.** No read-side case asserts "empty". One concrete row is held fixed and read three ways in the same boot: under the **org-less caller** the composed filter is the **deny sentinel specifically** (`RLS_DENY_FILTER`, not `undefined` and not an ordinary wall) and `matchesFilterCondition` says it **excludes** the row; under a **system context** the filter is `undefined` and the same row is **admitted**; with **one membership added** the sentinel becomes `{organization_id: 'org-1'}` which **admits** it. A row that was never written would be admitted by none of the three, so the system-context leg is the discriminator and the third leg rules out "denied to everyone but system".

**How a conforming 4xx was separated from any 4xx.** Every write case asserts `code === 'PERMISSION_DENIED'` **and** `statusCode === 403` **and** message content — that it names the missing active organization, and that it is **not** the sibling forge guard's "another tenant" sentence. The sharpest case: a caller with no org scope who *also* supplies a foreign `organization_id` trips both guards, both answer 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and only the message tells them apart.

### Cross-lane

**The fix itself hits no cross-lane wall — measured, not assumed.** My dispatch named `plugin-security` as a possible other lane, but the repo's own lane table (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`) puts `plugin-auth`, **`plugin-security`**, `plugin-sharing` and `plugin-audit` all under **`domain:identity`** — this card's own label. So both packages are in-lane and the rule's precondition is false. Recording it because the dispatch's example list said otherwise.

⚠️ **One CONSEQUENCE repair does reach another lane — reported, not absorbed.** See below.

### `Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3)` red on #8471 — analysis, with my confidence stated

One file, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-phantom-share-grant.dogfood.test.ts` (`beforeAll`, line 169): `admin creates the control note: expected 403 to be less than 300`. 34 other files passed in that shard; shards 1 and 2 green.

The setup is **#8208's scenario, exactly**: `bootStack(showcaseStack, { multiTenant: 'posture-only' })` (wall active), the harness admin — which #8208 measured as carrying *no `tenantId` at all* — doing `POST /data/showcase_private_note` over the real HTTP path. `showcase_private_note` declares `sharingModel: 'private'`, which is the row-ownership OWD, **not** `access.default: 'private'`; so it is an ordinary business tenant object and the ADR-0095 D3 platform-operator exemption correctly does not apply. That is the refusal working as declared, on a setup step that depends on the behaviour the ruling abolished.

⚠️ **Confidence: high on mechanism, NOT proven.** I grepped the CI log for my refusal's own marker (`Layer 0 tenant wall REFUSED`, `ADR-0123`, `no active organization`) and got **0 hits** — the server log is captured separately, so absence there is not evidence either way. Applying this card's own trap-2 discipline to my own diagnosis: a 403 alone does not prove it is *my* 403. The clean discriminator is already running — **#8473 has the same base and no plugin-security change; if its shard 3/3 goes green, the failure is mine; if it fails identically, it is pre-existing.** It was still `in_progress` at report time and I did not idle-poll it.

**If it is mine, the repair is one file, in `domain:cli` (`packages/qa`), and I have not touched it:** give the harness admin a membership before the control-note POST (create `sys_organization` + `sys_member` under the system context, then re-sign-in so `session.create.before` stamps it). Note #8473's ordering fix cannot do this for you here — `tenancy.defaultOrgId()` returns `null` under **any** walled posture by design, so nothing auto-binds under `posture-only`. **Irreducible per-lane surface: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-phantom-share-grant.dogfood.test.ts`, `beforeAll` only.** Your call whether I absorb it or it goes to the `domain:cli` seat.

**And if it is mine, it is also the HTTP-level closure of #8208 I said I had not measured** — CI reproducing, on the real stack, that the org-less admin's write is now refused instead of landing a NULL-org row.

### Gates — run with real results

Local, both branches: `pnpm --filter '<pkg>^...' build` (downstream-consumer direction not needed; no exported type narrowed), `typecheck` clean on both packages, **plugin-security 52 files / 1052 tests green**, **plugin-auth 52 files / 1186 tests green**, `check:adr-anchors` OK (48 anchored files), `check:nul-bytes` OK (7630/7631 files, no control bytes), `check:adr-0087-registration` OK (recognised the `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition), `check:changeset-no-major` OK, `check:error-code-casing` OK, `check:type-check-coverage` OK with **TEST_DEBT unmoved** (1533 frozen).

Remote at report time — #8471: `ESLint`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Check Changeset`, `Test Core (1-3/3)`, `Dogfood (1,2/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Core`, `Check PR Size`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue` all **success**; `Dogfood (3/3)` **failure** (above); `ADR maintainer approval` **failure — correct and expected**, it is the machine half of Prime Directive #14 and stays red until the maintainer approves. #8473: `ESLint`, `ADR maintainer approval` (**success**), `Dogfood (2/3)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/3)`, `Check Changeset` success; rest in progress.

**Gates I did NOT run locally, named:** the ~55 remaining `check:*` in the lint battery (`check:api-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:i18n*`, `check:react-blocks`, `check:liveness`, `check:generated`, …) — no `packages/spec` change, CI runs them once either way; `check:engine-double-contract` (neither test double declares `update`/`delete`, so the gate's subject does not exist — CI ran it anyway, green); `pnpm sdui:manifest` / `check:react-declaration-parity` (no objectui pin move); the full `pnpm test` / `pnpm typecheck` across all 77 packages.

### Answering the PM's two direct questions

1. **`ADR maintainer approval` on #8473: PASSES.** Confirmed both ways — the check run reports `success`, and the gate's governed surface is the literal prefix `docs/adr/` (`ADR_PATH_PREFIX`, `scripts/check-adr-merge-approval.mjs`), which `scripts/adr-anchors/*.json` does not match. Your correction is right: **only #8471 carries an ADR document**; #8473 can go through the normal flow.
2. **Duplicate-claim gate fixed.** Cause: #8471's body used a closing keyword in front of #8245 while *describing* #8473 — precisely the false-declaration trap the guard's own source comment warns about. Now: **#8471 declares #8208**, **#8473 declares #8245**, both `Part of #8247` (neither closes the decision card alone). The guard is **green on #8471**; #8473's re-run was triggered by a body edit.

### Out-of-scope finding filed

- **#8474** — `ADR-0081 D1` is cited in `auth-manager.ts` (×2) and in **ADR-0093** itself as the source of the default-active-org session hook, but `docs/adr/0081-*` is the trusted-react-page-tier record. `check:adr-anchors` cannot catch it (the number resolves to a *real* record; only its content is wrong), so it is green today and will stay green. Filed unassigned and unlabeled for triage; deduped against #8386, which is the same family and not a duplicate.

### What I could NOT verify

- Whether the #8471 dogfood failure is my refusal (mechanism-consistent, log marker absent, #8473's shard 3/3 is the discriminator and was still running).
- #8208's closure at the **HTTP** layer by a pin I wrote (only at the enforcement layer).
- Whether `single`/`group` postures reproduce #8208 on a real deployment — one of #8208's own open triage questions, untouched here.
- Post-report CI convergence on either PR (per the 2026-08-10 ruling, that wait is the PM's).

## Dev report — #8247, follow-up round (session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`)

```json
{
  "issue": 8247,
  "status": "done",
  "branch": "claude/issue-8247-no-active-org-semantics + claude/issue-8247-signup-membership-ordering",
  "pr": "https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/8471 (head 6e894de33) · https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/8473 (head 30b3ce6d7)",
  "premise_still_valid": true
}
```

Both consequences of the resolved discriminator are done, **in the order you asked for — evidence pinned first, red removed second.**

### 1. The measurement is recorded before it was erased

Committed as **`d498c6150`**, ahead of the fixture repair (`6e894de33`), so the record exists independently of the red ever having happened.

New pin: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/no-active-organization-write-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` — **6 cases, all green**, measuring #8208's scenario deliberately instead of as a side effect of someone else's setup:

| case | what it holds down |
|:--|:--|
| PRECONDITION | `tenancy` reports `posture: 'isolated'`, `isolationActive: true`, `degraded: false` — a degraded boot resolves to `single` where Layer 0 contributes nothing, so without this the file could be green and vacuous |
| PRECONDITION | the admin's resolved `tenantId` is `null` — #8208's own fact, re-measured |
| the refusal | `POST /data/showcase_private_note` → **403**, `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, message names the missing active organization |
| nothing landed | a system-context read (no wall narrows it) finds **zero** rows — the defect was a write that *succeeded* and then hid; a refusal that still landed the row would reproduce it while looking fixed |
| the control | **same caller, same object, same route SUCCEED** once a `sys_member` row exists and a fresh session is minted |

The control is the load-bearing one: `showcase_private_note` sits behind a CRUD/ownership gate that also answers `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` on that route, so without a leg where the identical request *succeeds* on one changed fact, the 403 would not be attributable to the missing organization at all. That is trap 2 applied to the pin itself.

Recorded on **#8208** as well, with the A/B that established attribution, so the card carries its own closure evidence rather than pointing at a PR body.

### 2. Fixture repaired — option A, declared not silent

`federated-phantom-share-grant.dogfood.test.ts`: the harness admin is bound to an organization before the first sign-in, so the setup step can reach the behaviour the file actually tests. **18/18 green.**

Bind-not-assertion-change on purpose: expecting 403 there would have deleted #8119's own control. Done by hand because there is no harness answer — `bootStack`'s `orgContext` **refuses** to compose with `multiTenant` (under a walled posture it would be a no-op that reads like a feature, the #7762 vacuity class), and #8473's ordering fix cannot help either since `tenancy.defaultOrgId()` returns `null` under **any** walled posture by design.

**Cross-lane declaration is in the PR body**, naming `packages/qa` as `domain:cli`'s surface, why both files are absorbed rather than handed over, and an explicit offer to split them out if that seat would rather own them. Absorbed-with-declaration, not absorbed-silently.

### 3. Blast radius — swept, not assumed

Rather than trust that one file was the only casualty, I ran **every** dogfood test that boots a walled posture: `attachments-permission-matrix`, `federated-anchor-provenance`, `federated-rls-injectors`, `org-create-default-team`, `rls-multitenant`, `showcase-external-autoconnect` — **5 passed, 1 skipped, 30 tests green**. Plus the repaired fixture 18/18 and the new pin 6/6. `federated-phantom-share-grant` really was the only one.

Re-run after the new files: `check:nul-bytes` OK (7632 files), `check:adr-anchors` OK (48 anchored files, 23637 citations resolve). `plugin-security` unit suite still 52 files / 1052 tests green.

### 4. `Fixes #8208` — kept, and now stronger than when I asked

Open question 2 closed itself exactly as predicted. The declaration was made on enforcement-layer evidence; it now rests on end-to-end evidence: the refusal fires over real HTTP, on this card's own scenario, and the pre-fix build let that write land. Both facts are pinned rather than narrated.

### One adjacent property, noted and deliberately NOT closed

Under `posture-only` — wall active *without* the enterprise organizations runtime — an **org-bound** caller's write still lands `organization_id: null`, because auto-stamping lives in that runtime and nothing in the open packages fills it. Visible in the control case above, where the control row lands with a null organization even though its creator has one.

Pre-existing, deliberate and documented at the stamping site ("a forged `org-scoping` registration yields NULL-org rows that the wall hides, i.e. a broken deployment rather than a working unlicensed one"), and a real walled deployment always has the stamper installed — so ADR-0123 D3 holds where it is meant to. Not introduced by this change, not in scope, and **not filed as an issue**: it is a declared packaging boundary rather than a defect. Flagging it because it is the one place the D3 wording ("no path may write a tenant-scoped row with a NULL tenant on behalf of an authenticated caller") is broader than what the open packages can enforce alone. If you want that gap tracked, say so and I will file it — I did not want to file a card against a decision that was made on purpose.

### Corrections — noted with thanks

Both of yours land, and neither cost anything: the lane-table check and the `adr-anchors`-vs-`docs/adr` distinction were both cheap to verify and would have been expensive to get wrong (one would have had me hand off in-lane work, the other would have parked a landable PR behind a human).

### Still not verified

- Post-report CI convergence on the new head `6e894de33` (per the 2026-08-10 ruling, that wait is yours). The local evidence is the scoped sweep above; the full farm is CI's.
- Whether a real (non-harness) deployment ever puts an admin in the no-active-organization state — #8208's own first triage question, untouched. What is settled is that the behaviour no longer depends on the answer.

## 两个 PR,以及为什么是两个

| PR | 内容 | 声明 | 状态 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **#8473** | 规则 2:首次会话成员时序(`plugin-auth`) | `Fixes #8245` · `Part of #8247` | **已入队** |
| **#8471** | 规则 1+3:ADR-0123 + fail-closed 写拒绝(`plugin-security`) | `Fixes #8208` · `Part of #8247` | ⛔ **等 maintainer** |

裁定要求「一次改动」,而拆分是**被迫且可测量**的,不是风格选择:

- `check:adr-anchors` 要求任何被跟踪文件里的 `ADR-NNNN` 必须指向 `docs/adr/` 下的真实记录,Prime Directive #13 要求实现 ADR 决策的代码带上它的 id ⇒ **规则 1 的执行引用 ADR-0123,无法与该 ADR 分离**,而 `docs/adr/**` 的 diff 按 Prime Directive #14 属于 maintainer。
- #8473 没有这层耦合:它立在**已接受**的 ADR-0093 上,不引用任何未合并记录,其对 #8245 的处置与 ADR-0123 最终措辞无关。

⚠️ 落地顺序恰好是有利的那个:**#8473 先减少「无 active org」状态在注册时出现的频率,#8471 才开始在该状态下拒绝写入。**

## ⚠️ ADR-0123 的 D3 有一处我方过度声明,已在合并前修正

原 D3 写的是「no path may write a tenant-scoped row with a NULL tenant on behalf of an authenticated caller」。

实测:在 **`posture-only`**(墙已激活但没有企业版 organizations runtime)下,**有 org 的调用者**写入仍然落 `organization_id: null` —— 因为自动打戳住在那个 runtime 里。这在 dev 自己的对照用例里可见:对照行落了 null-org,尽管其创建者有 organization。

⚠️ **这不是缺陷,是有意为之的打包边界**,打戳点自己的注释就写着:「a forged org-scoping registration yields NULL-org rows that the wall hides, i.e. a broken deployment rather than a working unlicensed one」。

**但裁定原文是有前件的**:「under an authenticated session with `activeOrganizationId == null` … ⛔ No silent NULL stamping **anywhere**」——那个 `anywhere` 约束的是**哪些层**受此规则(这正是一张因三个子系统各自即兴而立的卡的要害),它从未离开那个前件。而 D3 的句子**丢掉了前件**,于是承诺了关于每一个已认证调用者的事情。

所以 `5c36d7591` 修的是**我方的过度声明,恢复对裁定的忠实**,⛔ 不是收窄 maintainer 的决定:D3 的力度逐字保留(「in any subsystem … no layer gets an exemption from it」),另加一段作用域说明,并同样收紧了 TL;DR 那条,使摘要与决策不会漂移。D1、D2、D4 未动,没有增删或推翻任何决策。
